prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, industry and whether you need performance marketing, creative/brand work, product/UX, or a mix. I can shortlist strong candidates once I know more about what you need. Meanwhile, here’s a practical approach and a few well-regarded options organized by specialty.

Quick questions
- Primary goal: brand awareness, lead gen, e‑commerce growth, app installs, SEO, or something else?
- Monthly/annual marketing budget?
- Company stage/size (startup, SMB, enterprise)?
- Timeline (immediate campaign vs long-term partnership)?

Reputable agencies (San Francisco / strong presence in Bay Area)
- R/GA — large full‑service digital and experience agency. Good for brand transformation, large campaigns and enterprise work.
- AKQA — creative/product design and customer experience. Strong if you need UX/product design plus integrated campaigns.
- Huge — experience design and digital product development, good for brands that need site/app and marketing integration.
- Razorfish — digital marketing and tech-driven experience work; suited for enterprise clients with complex needs.
- 3Q Digital — performance marketing and paid media specialization (PPC, paid social, growth). Good for performance-driven acquisition.
- Wpromote — performance and growth marketing, strong in paid search/social and ROI-focused programs.
- Local boutiques and growth specialists — there are many smaller SF agencies (or growth consultancies) that are more affordable and nimble for startups and niche verticals.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Relevant case studies with measurable KPIs (CAC, ROAS, conversion lift).
- Experience in your industry or with companies at your stage.
- Clear reporting cadence and access to data (dashboards, attribution).
- Team structure and who will do the work vs. who will sell it.
- Pricing model (retainer, project, % of ad spend) and contract flexibility.
- Cultural fit and communication style.

Questions to ask prospective agencies
- What exact outcomes did you deliver for a similar client? Can you show metrics?
- Who will be on my account and what are their experience levels?
- How do you measure attribution and report performance?
- What tools/tech stack do you use? How is data shared?
- What does onboarding look like and how long to get results?

If you tell me your goals, budget and timeline I’ll shortlist 3–4 San Francisco agencies (one enterprise, one growth/performance, one boutique) and explain why each fits. Which would you prefer?
